name: WF-04 Recovery Planning
description: Onward Phase 5: given a validated incident and its operational impact, generates candidate recovery plans (repair via technician, replace asset, relocate operation) from real resource state (technicians/inventory/alternate locations), validates hard constraints deterministically, ranks only feasible plans, and persists every candidate (not just the winner) to recovery_runs/recovery_plans. Idempotent — skips replanning if a recovery_runs row already exists for the incident.
note: Published and live-gate-tested (Phase 5). Real evidence via a temporary webhook trigger (added and removed for this gate only, like WF-03's Phase 4 idempotency test) driving real n8n executions against real, directly-inserted incident/intelligence/impact rows plus real resource mutations: baseline (repair 28min/replace 19min infeasible vs 13min deadline, ROOM-208 7min feasible+recommended, ROOM-101 infeasible on capacity 50<84) exactly matches the Phase 5 brief's worked example; technician ETA 28->5 made repair feasible AND overtook relocation as the recommendation; ROOM-208 set unavailable made it fail specifically on location_status (not capacity/time) and yielded no_feasible_plan; people_affected raised to 150 made BOTH rooms fail specifically on capacity with status/capability/time all still passing; inventory setup_minutes 19->10 made replacement feasible and changed the plan set; a 3-minute deadline made all 5 candidates fail (no_feasible_plan, no fabrication); a 30-minute deadline produced 3 genuinely feasible plans ranked transparently by time (7 < 19 < 28) with 'X min slower than the recommended plan' reasons. Idempotency verified live: re-invoking for an already-planned incident took Already Planned? -> Existing Recovery in <1s without calling decision-engine again or creating a 6th recovery_plans row. Fingerprint verified live: two independent computations from identical resource state produced byte-identical state_fingerprint values; every resource mutation changed it. One real bug found and fixed during setup: Split Plans (splitOut, include:allOtherFields) keeps each split element nested under its ORIGINAL field name ('plans'), not spread onto the item root — Insert Recovery Plan's field mappings reference $json.plans.<field>. A second, more significant defect surfaced live and was fixed upstream (not in this workflow): Groq's required_capability output was free-form prose, never matching any real technician/inventory tag — fixed with a deterministic vocabulary clamp in decision-engine (app/schemas/incident.py's apply_review_policy), since Groq's own JSON-schema enum constraint proved unreliable for this model. 'Call Decision Engine' URL points at a Cloudflare Quick Tunnel (*.trycloudflare.com) — ephemeral, must be updated whenever the tunnel restarts, same as WF-02/WF-03. 'Fetch Alternate Locations' filters locations where transfer_minutes > 0 — selects real relocation targets and correctly excludes NULL (home/non-relocatable) rows under standard SQL null-comparison semantics. Hardening checkpoint: 'Call Decision Engine' URL updated to the current Cloudflare Quick Tunnel after runtime cleanup. Added retryOnFail (3 tries, 1s wait) to Fetch Incident, Check Existing Recovery, Fetch Intelligence, Fetch Impact, Fetch Technicians, Fetch Inventory, Fetch Alternate Locations, and Insert Recovery Run -- safe because recovery_runs.incident_id is a PRIMARY KEY. Insert Recovery Plan is DELIBERATELY left without retryOnFail: recovery_plans.id is a fresh generated UUID per candidate with no unique constraint tying it back to (incident_id, plan_type), so a spurious retry after a timeout-but-actually-succeeded write would create a genuine duplicate candidate plan row -- unlike every other write node in this system, this one has no DB-level protection against that (live node settings not re-serialized here in full; n8n is canonical per CLAUDE.md §9).

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ { incident_id: $('Fetch Incident').item.json.id, incident_capability: $('Fetch Intelligence').item.json.required_capability || null, operation_capability: $('Fetch Impact').item.json.affected_operations?.[0]?.required_capability ?? null, people_affected: $('Fetch Impact').item.json.affected_operations?.[0]?.people_affected ?? null, deadline_minutes: $('Fetch Impact').item.json.minutes_until_impact ?? null, technicians: $('Fetch Technicians').all().map(i => ({ id: i.json.id, name: i.json.name, skills: i.json.skills, status: i.json.status, eta_minutes: i.json.eta_minutes })), inventory: $('Fetch Inventory').all().map(i => ({ id: i.json.id, name: i.json.name, compatible_capability: i.json.compatible_capability, quantity: i.json.quantity, status: i.json.status, setup_minutes: i.json.setup_minutes })), alternate_locations: $('Fetch Alternate Locations').all().map(i => ({ id: i.json.id, code: i.json.code, name: i.json.name, capacity: i.json.capacity, capabilities: i.json.capabilities, transfer_minutes: i.json.transfer_minutes, status: i.json.status })) } }}
